name: What is a duplex property, and how does it differ from a single-family home?

mainEntity.name: What is a duplex property, and how does it differ from a single-family home?

acceptedAnswer.text: A duplex property consists of two separate dwelling units within a single building, sharing a common wall or floor. Each unit typically has its own entrance, kitchen, and bathrooms. Unlike a single-family home, which is designed for one household, a duplex offers two independent living spaces. This can be beneficial for homeowners looking for rental income to offset mortgage costs or for multi-generational living. Kelby Contreras can help you understand the specific zoning regulations and property types available in Miami-Dade and Broward Counties.
acceptedAnswer.description: A duplex has two independent dwelling units in one building, unlike a single-family home designed for one household.
